title: Generation and Distribution of Electricity
seo_title: Grade 10 Science: Generation and Distribution of Electricity Worksheets (MATATAG)
standard_code: Grade 10, Quarter 2: Force, Motion, and Energy
standard_text: Electricity is generated by electromagnetic induction in generators turned by turbines (steam, water, wind); transformers step voltage up for transmission and down for homes; alternating current; energy losses and efficiency. (summary of the MATATAG Science curriculum, Grade 10, Quarter 2: Force, Motion, and Energy)
meta_desc: Free Grade 10 Science worksheets (MATATAG, Quarter 2: Force, Motion, and Energy): electromagnetic induction, generators, transformers, transmission lines and alternating current. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: A changing magnetic field induces a current.
key_sub: High voltage reduces energy lost in power lines.
body_html:
How to think about it

In a power station, a turbine (turned by steam, falling water or wind) spins a coil in a magnetic field. The changing magnetic field induces an electric current: this is electromagnetic induction.

Transformers step the voltage up to very high values for transmission lines, which reduces the current and the energy lost as heat; then step it down for homes (230 V in the Philippines). The grid uses alternating current at 60 Hz.

Example

Why is electricity sent at high voltage?

P = IV; loss depends on current

Answer: a smaller current loses less energy as heat

Example

What does a step-down transformer do?

Before reaching homes

Answer: it lowers the voltage

Common mistakes

  • Thinking generators make energy from nothing.
  • Thinking transformers work with direct current.
  • Mixing up step-up and step-down transformers.
